 Patently Stupid is one of the games featured in The Jackbox Party Pack 5 . It's a drawing game, with the main concept being for the players to create an invention to solve ridiculous problems posed by their fellow players. And if you ever plan on calling the number on the advert , just skip the phone call and book your flight already!

 Contents

 1 Gameplay 

 2 Characters 

 3 Theme Song 

 4 Achievements 

 5 Promotional Art 

 6 Trivia 

 Gameplay [ ] 

 Patently Stupid begins with every player being given two fill-in-the-blank prompts. These will act as the problems the other players must solve with unique inventions. The problems are randomly sent out to everyone playing, and each player must choose a problem to create an invention for. Players start by drawing their invention, before giving it a title and a tagline to finish it all up. These inventions are then presented to the other players. For the sake of streaming the game, there is an option to have the hosts present for you, but, for playing in the same room as the other players, it's recommended to present the invention yourself for the full effect.

 Once every invention has been presented, the players can then invest on their favorite inventions using "money tokens," this game's score system. Each player has a $500 chip, a $300 chip and a $100 chip to award on 3 different inventions. The audience also votes on their favorite inventions, and the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd favorite receive $500, $300, and $100 from the audience, respectively. Players keep all money invested on their inventions. An invention that receives at least $1,000 (value may differ depending on player count) is considered "funded". The inventor of a "funded" invention will receive a $500 bonus, and everyone who invested in that invention will receive twice the money invested as return on investment.

 Each game consists of 2 rounds. In the second round, the highest ranking player will pick a problem from the problems not picked in the first round for all players to solve. The stakes are also higher: the funding chips are worth $800, $500, and $300, the funding goal is $1,500, and the funding bonus is $1,000.

 The highest score after two rounds wins.

 Patently Stupid is a party video game and one of five games featured in The Jackbox Party Pack 5 .

 Gameplay

 Firstly, all players will receive two fill-in-the-blank prompts on their device, revolving a certain problem, of which they'll have to type in whatever they want. After all of them have been submitted, they'll receive two problems from two other players, and they'll have to pick one of which they want to solve.

 Once everyone has chosen their problem, they'll then have to illustrate their idea on a cocktail napkin, of which they can draw on with a black pen and a marker that's the same color as their mug. They can also tap the "i" button at the top to see their prompt again if needed. When the drawings are in, the players will then be prompted to type in both a title and a tagline for their invention.

 Once everyone has finished drawing and writing their inventions, they'll then have to present them—they'll do this by either presenting it themselves, or have Toby and Lena present it for them instead. The latter can also happen if the player doesn't press either button for a couple of seconds.

 When all presentations have finished, everyone will be prompted to give out money tokens to three inventions they liked best, with descending cash amounts depending on their placement. Along with the voting, the players shall also fund at least $1,200 to earn a $500 funding bonus.

 Once all players have voted, all inventions pop up one by one, revealing the amount of cash they received by every player.

 If the funding succeeds, the player who earned the invention will earn their cash as well as the others who've funded said product, of which they'll receive double the cash listed in the money token they've given to said invention.

 If the funding fails, however, only the player who made the invention will earn the amount of cash they raised.

 In the final round , the player in first will choose one of the remaining problems on their device that they'll have every other player (along with themself) draw and write an invention for.

 The drawing and writing phases will work exactly the same as in the first round, as well as the voting phases, with the addition of higher money values and funding bars.

 At the end of both rounds, the player with the most cash overall will win the game.
